name: VISION Datasets
description: Despite progress in vision-based inspection algorithms, real-world industrial challenges -- specifically in data availability, quality, and complex production requirements -- often remain under-addressed. We introduce the VISION Datasets, a diverse collection of 14 industrial inspection datasets, uniquely poised to meet these challenges. Unlike previous datasets, VISION brings versatility to defect detection, offering annotation masks across all splits and catering to various detection methodologies. Our datasets also feature instance-segmentation annotation, enabling precise defect identification. With a total of 18k images encompassing 44 defect types, VISION strives to mirror a wide range of real-world production scenarios. By supporting two ongoing challenge competitions on the VISION Datasets, we hope to foster further advancements in vision-based industrial inspection.
evaluation_method: mAP for detection; mean IoU / Dice and pixel-level F1 for segmentation; per-class precision/recall where applicable
typical_sota_score: mAP typically ranges widely depending on dataset and defect type (roughly ~70–95% for easier defect categories; lower for small/rare defects)
reputation: Relatively recent but useful collection for industrial inspection tasks; gaining adoption through associated challenges and by researchers focused on manufacturing/defect-detection.
notes: Non-LLM, vision-only benchmark. Moderate overall size (~18k images) but pronounced class imbalance and per-defect variability; results vary strongly by defect type and imaging conditions. Masks provided across splits reduce annotation ambiguity but real-world deployment may reveal additional domain shifts.
